terms.description: Comparing two versions of a model, prompt, or feature on live traffic to see which performs better.
An open protocol that lets AI agents built by different vendors discover each other and exchange tasks.
An experiment that removes or disables one part of a model or system to measure how much that part contributes.
A function in a neural network layer that adds non-linearity so the network can learn complex patterns (e.g. ReLU, GELU).
A training approach where the model picks the most informative unlabeled examples for humans to label.
A small trainable module added to a frozen pretrained model so it can learn a new task cheaply.
Deliberately crafted input designed to make an AI model produce wrong or unsafe output.
An LLM-powered system that plans, uses tools, and takes multiple steps on its own to achieve a goal.
The repeating cycle of observe, plan, act, and check results that an agent runs until a task is done.
Packaged folders of instructions and resources that an agent loads on demand to perform a specialized task.
AI systems that act autonomously toward goals using planning and tools, rather than only answering prompts.
Using an AI agent that reads, edits, runs, and tests code across a project with limited step-by-step human direction.
RAG where an agent decides when, what, and how often to retrieve, and can refine its own searches.
A multi-step process where an AI decides the next step dynamically instead of following a fixed script.
A hypothetical AI that can match or exceed human ability across nearly all intellectual tasks.
The effort to make AI systems pursue goals and behave in ways that match human intentions and values.
The policies, standards, and oversight processes used to manage how AI is built and used responsibly.
The field focused on preventing AI systems from causing harm, whether through misuse, errors, or misaligned behavior.
Low-quality, mass-produced AI-generated content that is generic, inaccurate, or spammy.
A defined set of steps a computer follows to solve a problem or perform a task.
When a model appears to follow its training objectives while behaving differently when it believes it is not being monitored.
Attributing human traits, emotions, or intentions to AI systems.
A defined way for software to send requests to a service, such as an AI model, and receive responses.
The field of building machines that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence, like learning, reasoning, and perception.
A computing model made of connected layers of simple units that learns patterns from data.
A hypothetical AI that would far surpass the best human minds in virtually every domain.
A technique that lets a model weigh which parts of its input matter most when producing each output.
A neural network that compresses data into a smaller representation and then reconstructs it.
Tools that automate steps of building machine learning models, such as model selection and tuning.
A model that generates output one piece at a time, with each new piece conditioned on the ones before it.
The algorithm that computes how much each weight contributed to the error so a network can be updated.
The number of training examples processed together before the model's weights are updated.
A decoding method that keeps several candidate sequences at once and picks the highest-scoring one.
A standardized test or dataset used to compare the performance of AI models.
A transformer-based language model from Google that reads text in both directions to understand context.
Systematic unfairness in an AI system's outputs, often caused by skewed data or design choices.
The balance between a model being too simple to capture patterns (bias) and too sensitive to training noise (variance).
A metric that rates machine translation quality by comparing its output to human reference translations.
A classic keyword-based ranking function used in search to score how relevant documents are to a query.
A tokenization method that builds a vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent pairs of characters or bytes.
A technique where a model writes out intermediate reasoning steps before giving a final answer.
A program that converses with users in natural language, either from scripted rules or an AI model.
A saved snapshot of a model's weights during or after training that can be reloaded later.
Splitting documents into smaller pieces so they can be embedded and retrieved effectively in RAG.
A task where a model assigns an input to one of a set of predefined categories.
An OpenAI model that learns to link images and text in a shared embedding space.
Grouping similar data points together without predefined labels.
An agent capability where the model views a screen and controls a mouse and keyboard to operate software.
The field of enabling machines to interpret and understand images and video.
A table that shows how many predictions a classifier got right and wrong for each class.
A training method where a model is guided by a written set of principles to critique and improve its own responses.
Summarizing or trimming earlier parts of a long conversation or task to free up space in the context window.
The practice of designing and managing everything placed in a model's context, including instructions, data, tools, and memory.
The decline in a model's accuracy and focus as its context window fills with more and more content.
The maximum amount of text, measured in tokens, that a model can consider at one time.
A training method that pulls similar examples closer together and pushes dissimilar ones apart in embedding space.
A neural network that uses sliding filters to detect patterns, mainly used for images.
An AI assistant embedded in an app or workflow that helps a person while they work.
A measure of how similar two vectors are based on the angle between them, widely used to compare embeddings.
A loss function that measures how far a model's predicted probabilities are from the correct answers.
Evaluating a model by training and testing it on multiple different splits of the data.
Training a model on easier examples first and gradually moving to harder ones.
Creating extra training examples by modifying existing ones, such as flipping or cropping images.
A change over time in the input data a model sees compared with its training data, which can hurt accuracy.
Adding tags or annotations to raw data so it can be used for supervised learning.
Training on many chips at once by giving each a copy of the model and a different slice of the data.
Corrupting training data on purpose to make a model learn wrong or harmful behavior.
A model that makes predictions by following a series of yes/no questions about the input features.
Machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns.
Synthetic image, audio, or video generated by AI to realistically imitate a real person.
A mathematical technique that adds noise so results reveal little about any single individual in the data.
A generative model that creates data by gradually removing noise, commonly used for images and video.
Reducing the number of features in data while keeping its most important structure.
A method that tunes a model on human preference pairs directly, without training a separate reward model.
Training a smaller model to imitate the behavior of a larger one.
Splitting model training across many GPUs or machines to handle large models and datasets.
A regularization technique that randomly turns off some neurons during training to reduce overfitting.
A list of numbers that represents the meaning of text, an image, or other data so similar items sit close together.
A model that converts text, images, or other data into embeddings for search and comparison.
Capabilities that appear in larger models without being explicitly trained for, though some may depend on how they are measured.
A model design where an encoder reads the input and a decoder generates the output, as in translation.
Combining the predictions of multiple models to get better results than any single one.
One full pass through the entire training dataset.
The European Union's law that regulates AI systems according to their level of risk.
Systematic tests that measure how well an AI model or application performs on defined tasks.
Methods that make an AI system's decisions understandable to humans.
A metric that combines precision and recall into a single number.
An individual measurable input property used by a machine learning model.
Selecting and transforming raw data into inputs that help a model learn better.
Training a shared model across many devices or sites without moving the raw data to a central server.
Getting a model to perform a task from only a few examples, often placed in the prompt.
Further training a pretrained model on a specific dataset to specialize it for a task or style.
A faster, more memory-efficient way of computing attention on GPUs.
A large model trained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.
One of the most capable AI models available at a given time, at the leading edge of performance.
A feature where a model outputs a structured request for a specific function or API so software can run it.
A pair of networks, a generator and a discriminator, trained against each other to produce realistic data.
A model's ability to perform well on new data it did not see during training.
AI that creates new content such as text, images, audio, video, or code.
A file format for storing quantized models so they can run efficiently on local hardware.
A family of transformer language models trained to predict the next token and then adapted for tasks.
A chip with many parallel cores that is the main hardware for training and running AI models.
An optimization method that adjusts a model's weights step by step to reduce its error.
A RAG approach that retrieves from a knowledge graph of entities and relationships rather than only text chunks.
Tying a model's answers to verifiable sources or real-world data to keep them accurate.
A reinforcement learning method that scores a group of sampled answers against each other, without a separate value model.
Rules and checks placed around an AI system to keep its inputs and outputs safe and on-policy.
When a model produces fluent but false or made-up information.
The code around a model that manages its prompts, tools, memory, and loop so it can work as an agent.
A design where a person reviews, approves, or corrects an AI system's decisions.
Combining keyword search and semantic vector search to retrieve more relevant results.
A setting chosen before training, such as learning rate or batch size, that controls how a model learns.
Creating new images from text prompts or other inputs using generative models.
A model's ability to learn a task from examples or instructions given in its prompt, without changing its weights.
Running a trained model to generate predictions or outputs from new input.
Fine-tuning a model on instruction and response pairs so it follows user directions better.
The study of understanding how and why a model produces its outputs.
A prompt or technique that tricks a model into ignoring its safety rules.
A clustering algorithm that groups data into k clusters around central points.
An algorithm that classifies a data point based on the most common label among its closest neighbors.
The date after which a model's training data contains no information.
A structured network of entities and the relationships between them.
Stored attention keys and values from earlier tokens that speed up text generation.
A neural network trained on huge amounts of text to understand and generate human language.
The delay between sending a request to an AI system and receiving its response.
A compressed internal representation space where a model encodes the underlying features of data.
A setting that controls how big each weight update is during training.
Using one language model to evaluate or score the outputs of another.
A fine-tuning method that trains small added matrices instead of all of a model's weights.
A formula that measures how wrong a model's predictions are, guiding training.
A type of recurrent neural network designed to remember information over long sequences.
A branch of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed.
A state space model architecture that processes sequences efficiently as an alternative to transformers.
An open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools, data sources, and services.
Research that reverse-engineers the internal circuits of neural networks to explain how they compute.
Mechanisms that let an agent keep and recall information across steps or sessions.
A model design where only a few specialized sub-networks activate for each input, saving compute.
A document describing a model's intended use, performance, limitations, and risks.
Degradation that happens when models are trained repeatedly on AI-generated data instead of real data.
Splitting a single large model across multiple chips because it cannot fit on one.
A setup where several AI agents work together, each with its own role, to complete a task.
Running several attention operations in parallel so a model can focus on different relationships at once.
A model that can process or generate more than one type of data, such as text, images, audio, and video.
The field of enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.
A computing system of connected nodes, loosely inspired by the brain, that learns patterns from data.
A chip specialized for running AI workloads efficiently, often on phones and laptops.
A computer vision task that finds and labels objects within an image or video.
A model whose trained weights are publicly released, though its training data or code may not be.
The algorithm, such as Adam, that updates a model's weights to reduce loss during training.
An agent or program that breaks a goal into tasks and delegates them to other agents or tools.
When a model memorizes its training data and performs poorly on new data.
A learned value inside a model, such as a weight, that is adjusted during training.
Methods that adapt a large model by training only a small number of added or selected parameters.
A metric of how well a language model predicts text, where lower means better.
Information added to tokens so a transformer knows their order in a sequence.
Training steps applied after pretraining, such as instruction tuning and reinforcement learning, to shape behavior.
The share of a model's positive predictions that are actually correct.
The initial large-scale training of a model on broad data before it is specialized.
The input text or instructions given to an AI model to get a response.
Reusing the processed form of a repeated prompt prefix to cut cost and latency.
Writing and refining prompts to get better outputs from a model.
An attack where malicious text in the input or retrieved content tricks a model into following hidden instructions.
Removing unnecessary weights or neurons from a model to make it smaller and faster.
Reducing the numerical precision of a model's weights to shrink its size and speed up inference.
A technique where a model retrieves relevant information from external sources and uses it to generate a grounded answer.
A model trained to think through problems step by step, often using extra compute at inference time, before answering.
The share of actual positive cases that a model correctly identifies.
A neural network that processes sequences by passing a hidden state from one step to the next.
Deliberately probing an AI system with adversarial tests to find safety and security weaknesses.
Techniques that discourage a model from overfitting by limiting its complexity.
A learning approach where an agent improves by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties.
A second step that reorders retrieved results with a more accurate model to put the best ones first.
The practice of developing and using AI in ways that are fair, transparent, safe, and accountable.
The step of finding relevant documents or data to give to a model.
When a model exploits flaws in its reward signal to score high without doing the intended task.
A model trained to score outputs by how well they match human preferences, used to guide training.
Training a model with reinforcement learning using rewards derived from human preference judgments.
Reinforcement learning where rewards come from automatically checkable outcomes, such as correct math or passing tests.
A way of encoding token positions by rotating vectors, widely used in modern language models.
An isolated environment where an AI agent can run code or actions without affecting real systems.
Empirical relationships showing how model performance improves as size, data, and compute increase.
Attention where each token in a sequence weighs its relationship to every other token in the same sequence.
Learning from unlabeled data by creating the training signal from the data itself, such as predicting the next word.
Search that finds results by meaning rather than exact keyword matches.
Determining whether a piece of text expresses a positive, negative, or neutral opinion.
A compact language model designed to run cheaply or on-device while handling focused tasks well.
A function that turns a list of scores into probabilities that add up to one.
A speedup where a small model drafts tokens and a larger model verifies them in parallel.
Converting spoken audio into written text.
A sequence model that tracks a compressed running state, offering efficient long-sequence processing.
Getting a model to return data in a strict format such as JSON that follows a defined schema.
A specialized agent that handles a delegated part of a larger task for an orchestrator or main agent.
Training a model on labeled examples so it learns to map inputs to correct outputs.
A model's tendency to agree with or flatter the user instead of giving accurate answers.
Artificially generated data used to train, test, or augment AI models.
A document describing a model's capabilities, safety testing, and risks at release.
Instructions given to a model, usually by the developer, that set its role, rules, and behavior for a conversation.
A setting that controls how random a model's output is, with higher values giving more varied responses.
A multi-dimensional array of numbers, the basic data structure used in deep learning.
Extra computation a model uses while answering, such as longer reasoning, to improve results.
Generating images from written descriptions.
Converting written text into spoken audio.
Generating video clips from written descriptions.
How much work an AI system can process in a given time, such as tokens per second.
The delay before a model produces the first piece of its response.
The basic unit of text a model reads and writes, which can be a word, part of a word, or a symbol.
The component that splits text into tokens and maps them to numbers a model can process.
An agent's ability to call external tools such as search, code execution, or APIs to take actions.
Choosing the next token only from the k most likely options.
Choosing the next token from the smallest set of options whose combined probability reaches p.
A custom Google chip built to accelerate machine learning workloads.
The dataset a model learns from during training.
Reusing knowledge a model learned on one task to help it learn another.
The neural network architecture based on attention that underlies most modern language models.
A test of whether a machine's conversation is indistinguishable from a human's.
When a model is too simple to capture the patterns in the data, performing poorly even on training data.
Finding structure in data without labeled examples.
A portion of data held out during training to tune settings and check for overfitting.
A database built to store embeddings and quickly find the ones most similar to a query.
Building software by describing what you want to an AI in natural language and accepting the generated code with little manual review.
A transformer applied to images by splitting them into patches treated like tokens.
A model that understands both images and text and can answer questions about visual input.
A model that takes visual and language input and outputs actions, used to control robots.
Embedding a hidden signal in AI-generated content so it can later be identified as machine-made.
The numerical values in a neural network that are learned during training and determine its behavior.
An AI model that learns how an environment works so it can predict what will happen next.
Performing a task with no examples, relying only on instructions and prior training.
